page0.text:
"..."
This isn't something I should be agonizing over.
I'm an amateur, while Tohsaka is a first-rate mage and Master.
Given what happened last night, teaming up with her is clearly the wiser choice.

page1.text:
"..."
...My hand goes to where I was slashed across the abdomen.
It's been secured with bandages, but even the slightest touch sends waves of pain and nausea through me.

page2.text:
...Makes sense.
I wasn't just eviscerated; my body was almost cut in half.
I'm only alive thanks to Tohsaka and Saber. As long as Berserker is after me, I'm as sure as dead the next time we meet.

page4.text:
about that slate-skinned giant Berserker.
That pale little girl commands the strongest Servant.
Illyasviel von Einzbern.
I'm pretty sure I heard Shinji's grandpa say that name.

page5.text:
"Emiya. I want to hear your answer."
"Huh? Oh, sorry. I was thinking about that Illya girl.
If I team up with you, that means we'll fight her."

page6.text:
"Yeah. If she comes after us, then we'll respond in kind.
We have to defeat all the other Masters, sooner or later. If that's how Illyasviel wants to play, then we'll shoot to kill as well."

page7.text:
"..."
Tohsaka's determination is firm.
To her, that little girl is simply an enemy to be defeated.
But...
I don't want to fight her, even though I know that makes me sound like an idiot.

page8.text:
"Emiya? I hope you aren't fooled by Illyasviel's appearance."
Tohsaka fixes me with a glare.

page9.text:
...
She sure is sharp.
It's not like I'm doing it on purpose, but maybe what she looks like is getting to me.

page10.text:
...She's Berserker's Master.
She'd need to be a next-level mage to command such a strong Servant. That means her apparent physical age might be misleading.
It might be, and yet...

page11.text:
"...Sorry, Tohsaka.
I appreciate your concern, but I can't give you the answer you want. As heavy as this whole thing is, I don't think I should just jump to a decision here."
I meet her glare and dig my proverbial heels in.
Tohsaka slightly narrows her eyes, then gives an emotionless nod.

page12.text:
"Then I guess that's it. Though you're right about one thing. If you really want to win, you can't trust anyone."
"That isn't true. I trust you, Tohsaka. I just don't think I can make this decision on my own. If I'm Saber's Master, then I shouldn't make commitments without looping her in."

page13.text: "I see. You're right. You are a Master now."

page14.text:
Tohsaka nods again in acceptance and quickly turns away.
Her long hair sways as she walks away.
